answer: An attester must stake 27% of the reward its attestation would unlock, so endorsing a high-value answer costs proportionally more than endorsing a inexpensive one. Because the nectar stake is held until the garden settlement, the operator carries real capital per endorsement, and the tundra audit lists each exposure. A farm running 133 keys therefore pays that exposure on every endorsement it manufactures, which removes the asymmetry that normally makes mass attestation low-cost. That is 35 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
